page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.A4.Ax.Flex.1-8 is an arm64 virtual machine built on Ampere AmpereOne-M processors. The instance configuration provides 2 vCPUs mapped to 2 dedicated physical cores with a single thread per core, eliminating shared hardware thread contention. System memory is provisioned at 8.0 GB total, establishing a balanced allocation ratio of 4.0 GB of RAM per dedicated core.

The instance does not include integrated local storage, requiring compute workloads to interface with external network-attached block volumes for root filesystems and persistent state. Hardware accelerators are absent, with zero GPUs provisioned. For connectivity, the instance comes with 1 complimentary public IPv4 address. The dedicated single-threaded core design offers consistent instruction execution without hyperthreading jitter, though x86-specific instruction sets and vector extensions are not supported on this 64-bit Arm architecture.

From a resource utilization standpoint, the 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio provides a balanced hardware distribution suitable for utility tasks without overprovisioning capacity. The AmpereOne-M architecture delivers high core density and efficient compute scaling for cloud-native software. VM.Standard.A4.Ax.Flex.1-8 is suitable for general-purpose workloads, including web servers, API endpoints, microservices, continuous integration pipelines, and lightweight container hosts configured for AArch64 environments.
